conviction_note: Two small negatives on the reported quarter, both read off public filings: the -$0.04 EPS bar looks soft against Q3's operating run-rate, and revenue depends on a discretionary sale that management passed on at higher prices in Q3. They sum to -0.9. I emit -0.3, a third of that, because the stock is -26% in 20 days and 1.2% above its 52-week low on a sector-wide sell-off, calls are bid (skew -10.7), about 13.8% of float is short at ~6.5 days to cover, and UEC misses EPS so often (-18% average surprise) that some of this miss is expected.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue $9.0M and EPS -$0.04. Zacks (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:c1b414d12094b:0-uec-gears-up-to-report-q4-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/) and TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:afc01f5aa81d8:0-uec-q4-26-earnings-revenue-estimate-is-9-00m-usd/, https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:1c0320091f6df:0-uec-q4-26-earnings-eps-estimate-is-0-04-usd/) agree on both. Investing.com has EPS -$0.04 but revenue $6.71M (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/uranium-energy-faces-fiscal-year-test-as-spot-strategy-plays-out-93CH-4920568), so the EPS bar has three agreeing sources and the revenue bar two out of three. There is no company guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest 58.72M shares = 13.79% of float, 6.49 days to cover, from a Fintel/aggregator snippet with no settlement date (https://fintel.io/ss/us/uec; Fintel, Benzinga and Nasdaq pages returned 403/503, so this is snippet_only and unverified). Skew_25d is -10.73 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.51, event-implied move 7.7%. The stock is -26.2% over 20 days, -9.2% over 5 days, 54.6% off its high and 1.2% above its 52-week low. The drawdown is sector-wide: nuclear equities gave back the vote rally from 2026-09-18 and fell together on 09-23 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/18/nuscale-power-drops-7-as-nuclear-stocks-hand-back-the-vote-rally-oklo-falls-5-centrus-energy-slides-3/). Everything here argues for shrinking any negative.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26 (10-Q) opex was $40.8M: mineral property expenditures $29.5M, up from $15.7M, and G&A $9.4M. The Wyoming/Texas workforce went from 103 to 185 and construction is done in-house. Interest income was $4.2M. Q3's pre-mark loss was about $33M ($0.068/share on ~491M weighted shares); the other $0.04 of the -$0.11 was a $19.4M fair-value loss. If opex holds, the $9M consensus revenue at a ~$51/lb purchased-inventory cost basis ($73.9M / 1.456M lb) adds only ~$3.5M of gross profit. That puts Q4 near -$0.06 before marks, against a -$0.04 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print (2026-06-09 amc) missed EPS at -$0.11 vs -$0.03 with zero revenue: -11.55% (baseline; https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/06/53082430/uranium-energy-reports-q3-results-with-wider-eps-loss-shares-slide). The 2026-03-10 print was in line on EPS with about 2x the revenue estimate and moved -2.28% (baseline). Misses get sold and beats do not get bought. Zacks puts the average EPS surprise at -18%, so misses are habitual.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates have been flat for 30-60 days and the Zacks ESP is 0.00%, so nobody has moved the EPS number toward the Q3 run-rate. If the street had, consensus would sit near -$0.06 to -$0.07, not -$0.04. Two things reduce the size. The market knows UEC misses habitually. And below-the-line items can offset: URC closed its Sweetwater Royalties combination on 2026-07-27, cutting UEC's stake from 12.3% to 7.7%, which could book a dilution gain like the $3.46M already recorded (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1334933/000143774926019889/R13.htm). The Anfield mark looks like only about -$3M.
findings.independence: The Zacks preview says higher exploration and G&A spending, driven by workforce additions, would 'offset the increase in revenues' (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:c1b414d12094b:0-uec-gears-up-to-report-q4-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/). The workforce figure comes from the Q3 call (https://equibles.com/stocks/uec/calls/2026-q3). Both read the same opex trend as the 10-Q, so this is weak independence.

findings.finding: Revenue depends on a discretionary sale from inventory, and the tape was against one. On the Q3 call management said it 'preserved our inventory' in flat prices, when the April-end mark was about $87/lb ($127M / 1.456M lb). Zacks puts the May-July spot average at $85.19/lb, below that level and far below the $101/lb of the Q2 sale. A second zero-revenue quarter against the $9M bar is a live outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Zero revenue in Q3 FY26 (together with the EPS miss): -11.55%. Revenue about 2x the estimate in Q2 FY26 ($20.2M from 200k lb at $101): -2.28% (baseline; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/uranium-energy-corp-reports-results-for-second-quarter-of-fiscal-2026-302708835.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Zacks and TradingView carry $9M of revenue, unchanged for 30 days. If the street had absorbed management's no-sale-in-flat-prices behaviour and the lower Q4 tape, the bar would sit near $0-5M. Investing.com's $6.71M suggests part of the street already models lighter sales, which is why this is sized small. It is also an inference about a decision, not a disclosed number.
findings.independence: The inventory valuation and pound counts come from the Q3 release (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/uranium-energy-corp-reports-results-for-the-third-quarter-of-fiscal-2026-302794776.html) and the spot average from Zacks (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:c1b414d12094b:0-uec-gears-up-to-report-q4-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/). This finding shares the $9M revenue input with finding 1, but it rests on a different fact (the sale decision rather than opex), so it counts separately. If both are true they compound rather than contradict.

outside_window.finding: The UR&C conversion facility's Class 4 cost study, and with it site selection, was guided on the Q3 call to the first half of calendar 2027. That caps how far a refinery headline on 09-29 can go beyond naming a site.

searched_and_found_nothing: Company press releases since June: only the AGM results (07-23) and the date notice (09-22). No operational, contract, DOE or UR&C-site news. https://www.uraniumenergy.com/news/releases/2026/index.php

EDGAR since the 10-Q (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001334933.json): 8-K 07-23 is the AGM. The 07-31 and 08-03 Form 4s are annual RSU/option grants and vestings at a $9.74 strike (no open-market sales); the 4/As amend 2023 vesting reports; the 13D of 07-27 covers the URC stake (28.97M shares, 7.7%) after URC's Sweetwater Royalties combination. No 424B filings since Nov 2025, so ATM usage after the 494.87M-share 10-Q cover count cannot be seen before the 10-K.

The 10-Q commitments note: FY25's 300k lb of purchase commitments at $37.05 were for FY26 delivery, and inventory rose 100k lb net of the 200k lb Q2 sale, consistent with delivery by April. The Q3 10-Q R-pages showed no remaining commitment or sales contract. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1334933/000143774926019889/R9.htm

Backing UEC production out of EIA's Q2 2026 US total (1,087,504 lb; https://www.eia.gov/uranium/production/quarterly/) using Energy Fuels (865k lb finished) and Ur-Energy (140.9k lb drummed). This leaves about 82k lb for four facilities including enCore, which is inconsistent with enCore's own 131k lb extraction. The definitions differ, so the proxy was dropped. Hobson (Texas) is not among EIA's six producing facilities for Q2, so Burke Hollow pounds were probably not yet drummed by June.
Uranium spot tape: ~$90/lb flat through September, so there is no new tape shock into the print.
Anfield equity mark: about CA$6.09 on 07-17 vs US$5.00 at April-end, roughly -$3M, which is immaterial.
Short-interest primary pages (Nasdaq, Fintel, Benzinga) returned 503/403.
baseline_tension: Both findings are negative, against call skew of -10.7, a 26% 20-day drawdown to a 52-week low and ~14% of float short. They cut against the option market and the positioning, so the emitted number is a third of the findings' sum. The drawdown itself is sector beta, not company news.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning): both findings are negatives against a -10.7 call skew and ~14% short interest at a 52-week low. Shrank F1 from -1.0 to -0.6 and F2 from -0.5 to -0.3, and the expected move from -0.6 to -0.3.

Lesson 5 / 'documents beat inference': F2 is an inference about a discretionary sale decision, not a disclosed number, so it stays the smaller of the two. F1 is a cost walk read off the 10-Q, so it is kept.

Lesson 2 (one-offs): the URC dilution gain and the Anfield mark are below the line and could offset part of the F1 EPS gap. This was stated in F1's why_not_priced and folded into its reduced size rather than filed as a separate finding.

Lesson 6 (bar): EPS -$0.04 has three agreeing sources. Revenue $9M has two agreeing and one dissenting ($6.71M), so it is sized as sourced but small. Both findings resolve on the 09-29 print, and the UR&C 2027 study was moved to outside_window.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): the history shows misses sold (-11.55%) and a 2x revenue beat sold (-2.28%), so the reaction function does not veto a negative. It left the signs standing.
